t: Make Costs of Paths Equal in a Binary Tree — Bottom-Up Normalization
o: Increments only; make all root-to-leaf path sums equal, minimizing total increments. Work bottom-up: once both subtrees of a node are internally consistent (all their leaf paths equal), the two subtree totals may differ; raise the smaller side to match the larger — the difference must be paid as increments somewhere in that subtree, and paying it as high as possible is free (it fixes all leaves below uniformly). At each internal node add |leftTotal - rightTotal| to the answer and return cost[node] + max(leftTotal, rightTotal).
k: Process bottom-up: normalize each subtree so all its leaf-path sums are equal.
At each internal node, the imbalance |L - R| must be added to the smaller side — charge it once to the answer.
Returning max(L, R) + own cost propagates the minimal consistent subtree total.

a.n: Approach 1: Post-order DFS on the perfect tree
a.i: Children of node i (1-indexed) are 2i and 2i+1. Recursive function returns the required equal path-sum contribution of the subtree; accumulate absolute differences at every internal node.
s: Define dfs(i): if i > n return 0.
l = dfs(2i), r = dfs(2i+1); ans += |l - r|.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def minIncrements(self, n: int, cost: List[int]) -> int:
        import sys
        sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)
        ans = 0
        def dfs(i):
            nonlocal ans
            if i > n: return 0
            l = dfs(2 * i)
            r = dfs(2 * i + 1)
            ans += abs(l - r)
            return cost[i - 1] + max(l, r)
        dfs(1)
        return ans

a.t: O(n) — each node visited once in post-order.
a.sp: O(h) = O(log n) — recursion depth of the perfect tree.

a.i: Avoid recursion by processing the array from the deepest level upward: for sibling pairs (2i, 2i+1) at each level, add their difference to the answer and replace both with their max plus the parent's cost, collapsing levels until the root.
s: Iterate i from n/2 down to 1 (internal nodes in reverse).
a.t: O(n) — one reverse pass over internal nodes.
a.sp: O(1) extra — mutates the cost array in place.

w: The iterative version is safest in interviews (no recursion-limit worries) and elegantly exploits the array-encoded perfect tree. Pitfalls: 64-bit accumulation (path sums up to ~1e4·17 per level, totals fit in long), 1-indexed vs 0-indexed confusion, and forgetting that only increments are allowed (so we raise to max, never lower to min). Follow-up: allow decrements too (answer becomes half-ish — actually then equalize to any common value optimally via medians per root-path), or a non-perfect tree.
